title: US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC
snippet:
The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. About one in 10 children under age 5 have been hospitalized.

About 93% of cases are among people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown, CDC data shows. [...] Meanwhile, 3% of cases are among those who have received just one dose of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine and 4% of cases are among those who received the recommended two doses, according to the CDC. [...] "Crossing this threshold is a tragic reminder that measles has made an alarming comeback in the United States," Dr. Richard Besser, former acting CDC director during the Obama administration, said in a statement to ABC News. "As a pediatrician and a parent, it breaks my heart that so many children are suffering needlessly from a dangerous and potentially fatal disease that vaccines can prevent. It represents a profound moral failure on the part of our national health leaders."

title: US sees highest number of measles cases in 35 years
snippet:
# US measles cases reach 35-year high

Getty Images A fact sheet for measles sits on a table with a dark blue tablecloth, in a clipboard

The US has hit a 35-year high in measles cases, according to new figures from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The US has seen 2,318 confirmed cases of measles in 2026, just seven months into the year, up from last year's high of 2,289, when two unvaccinated children died of the disease. [...] Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has been criticised by public health experts who argue his remarks and remaking of US vaccine policy has hindered efforts to stop the outbreaks.

A vaccine skeptic, Kennedy has shared mixed messaging on the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine, which has been proven safe and effective.

The US recommends two shots to children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness. [...] The rising number of cases have come as vaccine hesitancy in the US has increased in recent years, leading to lower immunisation rates.

In November, a panel is set to decide whether the US will lose its status of having eliminated measles, which Canada lost last year.

A country loses elimination status after a year or more of continuous transmission of the same strain of the measles virus.

title: US measles cases reach 35-year high, for second record-breaking year in a row
snippet:
Measles has continued its historic resurgence in the United States this year, with a second record-breaking year in a row. Just over halfway through 2026, the country has recorded more cases than in any other year since 1991 – surpassing a grim milestone that was just topped last year.

The disease was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, but more cases have been recorded in the past 18 months than there have been in the previous 25 years combined. [...] Most of the cases in 2026 have been associated with outbreaks that started last year — like in South Carolina, where the outbreak extended through late April. An outbreak along the Utah-Arizona state line has been simmering for more than a year, a key milestone that international health officials will assess when they meet in November to discuss whether the US can still claim to have measles elimination status. [...] South Carolina has reported more measles cases in 2026 than any other state. An outbreak started raging across Spartanburg County in October; it would become the largest the largest the US has seen in decades, with nearly 1,000 cases, before ending in April this year.

Geographically speaking, the Rev. Scott Neely’s Unitarian Universalist Church of Spartanburg was right in the center of the outbreak.

title: Measles Cases Hit New Record in U.S., as Vaccination Rates Wane
snippet:
The United States has now recorded more cases of measles in 2026 than in any other year since the virus was declared eliminated in 2000, a grim sign that the country may be headed toward a new era in which the disease regularly sickens thousands every year. [...] On Friday, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced that there have been 2,318 confirmed cases of measles so far this year. The case count toppled the record set last year, when measles infected more than 2,200 Americans and killed two unvaccinated children. More measles cases have been reported in the United States in the last two years than in all the years from 2000 through 2024 combined. [...] Measles Outbreaks

title: U.S. measles cases hit 35-year record with months left in 2026
snippet:
# U.S. measles cases hit 35-year record with months left in 2026

Data from Johns Hopkins University’s U.S. measles tracker shows the nation reported 2,295 cases as of Tuesday. That count surpasses last year’s total of 2,289.

The United States has now reported the most measles cases in any year since 1991, not only surpassing all of last year’s record total, but also reaching the highest level in 35 years, with more than five months still remaining in 2026.
